Julian — thanks, got the docs. Quick answers and proposed next steps below.

Short answers:
- SCCs: Redwood will rely on the EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (processor-controller set) for this relationship; we'll include an executed Annex that reflects NovaMed-specific routing commitments.
- Hosting/region: Hosted customers may choose region pinning; for this deal we will pin EU residency (Frankfurt region) for customer data, with our cross-border fallback described in the attached DPA redline.
- Evidence bundle (minimal for TIA): SOC 2 Type II report (last 12 months), encryption-at-rest diagram with key management notes, KMS vendor and rotation policy summary, current subprocessor roster (latest CSV), and our data flow diagram. See suggested file list attached (evidence_inventory.csv).

On section 5.2: we flagged the ambiguity too — we've suggested language that clarifies when Redwood can engage subprocessors for cross-border routing and the notification/window for objections. See attached redline_dpa_v2.docx (I edited the clause to add a 10-business-day review window).

Proposed timeline:
- Today: we deliver DPA redline + evidence inventory (attached).
- Tue 9/5: legal call with NovaMed counsel to walk the DPA redline (30 minutes).
- Wed 9/6: Redwood provides SOC2 + diagrams via S3 link and shares subprocessor contracts excerpt for top-3 subprocessors.
- Thu 9/7: final sign-off window (DocuSign request) if no open objections.

If that timeline works, I will put Ben and Laura on the call for the technical and commercial points.

Best,
Soojin

Team — quick internal note and suggested response to NovaMed counsel: 

1) Localization commitment: commercial is okay to add an Order Form clause: "Primary customer data for EU NovaMed accounts will be hosted in the EU region (Frankfurt) for a minimum of 24 months following contract execution unless otherwise agreed in writing." Ben — please confirm this does not materially change pricing or capacity assumptions.

2) Subprocessor onboarding / objection: we can accept a 10-business-day review window with an explicit remediation path. Proposed language: "Customer may object to a proposed subprocessor within 10 business days of notice; Redwood will pause onboarding of the subprocessor and engage in a good-faith remediation period of up to 15 business days to address Customer objections. If unresolved, the parties will escalate to the named privacy leads for arbitration." Laura — please confirm the escalation and timing language is acceptable from a legal risk perspective.

3) Evidence handoff: SOC2 and diagrams will be shared via expiring S3 link by EOD 9/6. We will also provide a subprocessor excerpt bundle (redacted contracts) for the top-3 subprocessors.

If Ben and Laura sign off on the two language tweaks below, I'll send updated Order Form and DPA redlines and instruct Procurement to initiate DocuSign (link included). Otherwise propose a 30-minute call tomorrow 9/8 to resolve.

Proposed attachments to include in the response: redline_dpa_v2.docx, evidence_inventory.csv, and a one-page Order Form amendment showing the 24-month localization clause.

Soojin
